record.paper_title: Open problems originated in our research work with Zoltán Daróczy
record.context_brief: Completely additive functions and interval-containing subset sums
record.original_question: Let {λ_n} be a nonincreasing sequence of positive numbers with L_n=λ_{n+1}+λ_{n+2}+⋯<∞ for every n, and let H={x : x=∑_{n≥1} ε_nλ_n with ε_n\in\{0,1\}}. Assume H contains an interval. Suppose (a_n)\in l_1 has the property that for every choice of coefficients δ_n\in\{-1,0,1\}, the relation ∑ δ_nλ_n=0 always implies ∑ δ_n a_n=0. Must the ratio a_n/λ_n be constant for all n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4. Let {λn}be a sequence of positive numbers for which λn ≥ λn+1 (n = 1 , 2, . . .) such that Ln = λn+1 + · · · < ∞. Assume that H = { x | x = ∑∞ n=1 εnλn, ε n ∈ { 0, 1} } contains an interval.
Assume furthermore, that {an}∞ n=1 ∈ l1 is such a sequence for which ∑ δnλn = 0 δn ∈ {−1, 0, 1} always implies that ∑∞ n=1 δnan = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{\lambda_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ be a nonincreasing sequence of positive real numbers such that 
$$L_n = \sum_{k=n+1}^{\infty}\lambda_k < \infty \quad \text{for every } n\geq 0,$$
and define
$$H = \Big\{ x \in \mathbb{R} : x = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon_n \lambda_n,\ \varepsilon_n \in \{0,1\} \Big\}.$$
Assume that $H$ contains a nondegenerate interval. Suppose $(a_n)_{n\geq 1} \in \ell_1$ has the property that, for every sequence $(\delta_n)_{n\geq 1}$ with $\delta_n \in \{-1,0,1\}$,
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\delta_n \lambda_n = 0 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\delta_n a_n = 0.$$
Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, the ratio $a_n/\lambda_n$ must be the same constant for every $n\geq 1$.
